complete_sample_holdout.interpretation: Independently estimated on disjoint sample halves the covariate-richness rank correlation keeps its sign and magnitude, so the association is a property of the sample population rather than of any particular subset.

feature_holdout.interpretation: Disjoint feature halves reproduce the same covariate association and the same positive richness-depth coupling, so the structure is distributed across the feature set rather than carried by a few features. Note this is a feature split for variance structure only; as the data guide warns, feature-level splits are not valid for composition-level validation.

scenario_holdout.interpretation: A condition_2 -> condition_3 calibration fitted in one scenario transfers to the other with negative out-of-sample R2 and a large mean bias, so the relation direction is scenario-specific and must not be pooled across scenarios.

explanation_families.interpretation: Over the 400 metric ids shared by both scenarios the zero/non-zero indicator of condition_2 carries at least as much association with condition_3 as any continuous specification: +0.478 in high_variance against a rank specification of +0.459. The ratio specification is undefined on 0.195 of small_sample cells and 0.465 of high_variance cells, and negative where defined; a log transform of condition_2 is rank-identical to the raw values. The best-supported description of the relation is a level shift between cells where condition_2 is exactly zero and cells where it is positive, not a monotone dose-response. Note that the presence of a large negative ratio correlation conditional on c2 > 0 is the expected arithmetic consequence of the c3 > c2 ordering, not a separate scientific effect.

monotonicity.interpretation: A monotone (isotonic) fit earns a real out-of-sample gain over a straight line (0.431 vs 0.133 cross-validated R2), and an 8-bin step function matches it (0.409), while the octile medians rise only across the lower half of the covariate range and then flatten with local reversals. The supported statement is a positive, concave, saturating association - steeper below the covariate median (about 16) than above it - not a proportional one.

covariate_domain.note: The covariate mixes small fractional values (0.03, 0.25) with large integers (36, 42, 83.2) across a roughly 2800-fold range, so it is treated throughout as an ordinal/rank variable rather than an interval one.
